preconditions.description: Contract must have BNB balance (from accumulated fees) or other ERC20 tokens from previous recoverTokens calls

violation_target.exploit_hint: Call the clearStuckBNB() function directly as any address to drain all BNB from the contract to the caller. The function lacks the onlyOwner modifier, allowing anyone to transfer the contract's BNB balance to themselves. No special roles or token balances required.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The clearStuckBNB() function lacks proper access control. It only has a tautological check require(_msgSender() == _msgSender()) which always passes, allowing any caller to drain the contract's BNB balance to themselves.
attempts.attack_strategy: Directly call the clearStuckBNB() function from the attacker's address to drain all BNB from the contract.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the initial BNB balance of the attacker. 2. Call clearStuckBNB() on the target contract. 3. Verify the attacker's BNB balance increased.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is real - clearStuckBNB() allows anyone to drain BNB, but the contract needs to have BNB first. We can simulate this by giving the contract BNB using the deal() cheatcode.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Use deal() to give the target contract some BNB. 2. Call clearStuckBNB() to drain it to the attacker. 3. Verify the attacker received the BNB.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Give the target contract 10 ETH using deal(). 2. Record attacker's initial balance. 3. Call clearStuckBNB(). 4. Verify attacker's balance increased by approximately 10 ETH.
attempts.failure_reflection: The contract had zero BNB balance, so calling clearStuckBNB() didn't transfer any funds. We need to first ensure the contract has BNB to drain.
